subtype: Approach: planning a visit with a shared budget [Action]
passage: Dilnaz and Hrithik sat over one spreadsheet, her in Mumbai, him in Pune, by video. Column A: train fare, both ways. Column B: two nights in a small guest house. Column C: food. Hrithik added: "That comes to about the same as a month of my allowance." "So we alternate. This visit I pay the train and you pay the stay. Next time swap." "Fair." Dilnaz added a line at the bottom: "Small tin, five hundred a month each, for visits only." They decided on the date, the 17th, because neither had a test. Hrithik looked at the sheet, and at her. "It's our first real plan." "It's a weekend," Dilnaz smiled. "But it's a start." She saved the file as "Visit 1".

qa.q: On which date did Dilnaz and Hrithik decide to meet?
What is Hrithik feeling when he calls it their first real plan?
qa.a: Hrithik feels moved and hopeful, looking at the sheet and at her as the visit becomes concrete.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the pair use if money gets tight, and why?
qa.a: They could plan a shorter or closer meeting or use an existing free day, because a smaller visit keeps the promise without straining either budget.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz see the visit plan?
qa.a: Dilnaz calls it just a weekend but a start, and saves the file as 'Visit 1', so she seems to treat it as the first of several trips.

grounding: Shows a couple planning a visit with costs written down, taking turns paying, and putting aside a small regular amount.

subtype: Approach: planning a visit with a shared budget [Action]
passage:
'Okay, sleeper train from Bhopal to Pune: 640 each way. So 1,280 for me,' Hafsa said, reading from her laptop.
'Hostel guest room's 500 a night. Two nights, 1,000,' Chinmay said. 'Food, maybe 800 if we're sensible.'
'So 3,080 for the weekend.'
'This time I'll cover the room and food. You're doing the train.'
'And next time you come to Bhopal, you do the train and I handle the rest?'
'Deal. Turns.' He paused. 'That's still a lot for March.'
'That's why I made this.' Hafsa turned the screen: a small table. 'If we each keep aside 700 a month from our allowances, by March it's there and we don't have to ask anyone.'
'You made a sheet for us.'
'I made a sheet for us.'
He laughed. 'Put me down for 700. And add a line for chai on the platform.'

qa.q: How much is the sleeper train each way?
Why did Hafsa make the sheet, and how might she feel when Chinmay laughs and agrees?
qa.a: She wanted the visit to happen without strain on either of them, and she likely feels relieved and happy that he is on board.

qa.q: What else could Hafsa and Chinmay consider if the plan feels tight?
qa.a: They could talk it through again and pick a smaller option, like one night instead of two, or ask a trusted family member for advice.

qa.q: How might the sheet look to Chinmay?
qa.a: It surprises and touches him, showing that Hafsa is planning for both of them, so the visit feels shared rather than a burden on one person.

grounding: Shows a couple working out train, stay and food for a weekend visit, taking turns to pay, and each setting aside a small monthly amount.

subtype: Approach: planning a visit with a shared budget [Action]
passage:
The first time I visited Arvind in Chandigarh, I spent so much in two days that I ate hostel dal for the rest of the month and felt resentful the whole time. I'm Deepika, and I didn't want the second visit to go like that.
So on a call in January we listed everything: bus fares both ways, a guesthouse for two nights, food, one outing. My roommate Himani, who is good with sheets, helped me set it out in columns. We agreed on turns: I would pay the bus this time and he'd cover the stay; next time, the other way round. We also each put a small amount aside every month from our allowances, in a jar we photograph for each other.
In April the visit happened. We knew the numbers before I boarded, nobody had to ask for money at a counter, and I came home still able to afford the canteen.

qa.q: What did Deepika and Arvind list on the January call?
qa.a: Bus fares both ways, a guesthouse for two nights, food, one outing.

qa.q: How did Deepika feel after the first visit, and why?
qa.a: Deepika felt resentful and stretched after spending so much that the rest of the month was hostel dal.

qa.q: What else could the couple do before the next visit?
qa.a: Go over the sheet together a week before and agree on any changes, so neither is surprised at a counter.

qa.q: How might the jar photos feel for Arvind?
qa.a: They let Arvind see that both are putting in, which likely makes the visits feel fair and shared.

grounding: Shows a couple listing fares, stay and food for a visit, taking turns to pay and each setting aside a little from allowances each month.
